quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): FY26/6 orders received reached a record JPY 324.2 billion, up JPY 98.7 billion YoY. Semiconductor & Electronics orders rose JPY 42.9 billion - logic on a sharp increase in orders for MHM (Metal Hard Mask) systems for China in H2 plus firm advanced-node demand; memory as investment by the three major DRAM manufacturers expanded on growing HBM demand, with investment by a North American manufacturer making a particularly significant contribution; packaging on continued strong demand for ashing equipment for WLP and the start of full-scale investment in PLP mass-production development. Display & Energy rose JPY 20.5 billion (LCD modification and capacity expansion, G8 OLED investment concentrated among major manufacturers, strong Chinese market). General Industrial rose JPY 29.0 billion (expanding rare-earth-related orders, leak test systems reclassified from Components, Customer Support growth).
quarterly_data.figure: orders JPY 324.2 billion (+JPY 98.7 billion YoY); Semiconductor & Electronics +JPY 42.9 billion, Display & Energy +JPY 20.5 billion, General Industrial +JPY 29.0 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): FY26/6 one-time impact totalled JPY 5.8 billion - approximately JPY 2.3 billion in Q3 (mainly an allowance for doubtful accounts in SG&A for EV-related expenses) and approximately JPY 3.5 billion in Q4 in cost of sales. Breakdown: a revenue timing shift in Semiconductor of JPY 1.4 billion (because of customer-side factors, revenue recognition of a large acceptance-based project shifted from Q4 to the next fiscal year), EV-related expenses of JPY 3.7 billion, and quality verification remediation of JPY 0.7 billion (inspection equipment issues in the Materials business). Management says these will have no impact on FY27/6 and it is not aware of other material risks, including impairment losses.
quarterly_data.figure: one-time impact JPY 5.8 billion (revenue timing shift JPY 1.4 billion, EV-related JPY 3.7 billion, quality remediation JPY 0.7 billion)

quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): the FY27/6 forecast incorporates the reduction from business reform - approximately JPY 28.6 billion less in orders received, approximately JPY 20.0 billion in net sales and approximately JPY 1.5 billion in operating profit - and, although the year began with an order backlog of JPY 176.1 billion, it reflects delays in recognizing sales and profit due to extended parts and materials procurement lead times; management calls the overall forecast conservative.
quarterly_data.figure: business-reform reduction approximately JPY 28.6 billion orders, JPY 20.0 billion net sales, JPY 1.5 billion operating profit; opening backlog JPY 176.1 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): demand related to AI data centers continues to expand, but equipment lead times are lengthening. Semiconductor production equipment lead times have lengthened by approximately two to three months from around six months (orders received without prior forecasts made advance arrangement of parts difficult, and strong demand lengthened procurement lead times); display equipment lead times remain approximately one year; rare-earth-related equipment lead times are expected to exceed one year. Procurement lead times are extending for electronic modules used broadly in semiconductor production equipment and for rare-earth magnets used in components such as pumps; the company is using common purchasing with suppliers and adopting alternatives, aiming to normalize lead times within approximately six months to one year. Uncertainty is increasing over smooth procurement of rare earths and other materials from China; tariffs are generally borne by buyers, with no notable change in customer orders.
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor equipment lead times lengthened approximately two to three months from around six months; normalization targeted within approximately six months to one year

quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on FY27/6 semiconductor investment: logic investment is expected to stay high; orders from China are conservatively expected broadly in line with the previous year; for advanced processes, investment by the Taiwanese foundry and other customers remains firm and the plan includes certain projects for the North American logic maker. Strong HBM demand will remain a powerful tailwind for memory, with DRAM investment by the three major manufacturers driving growth; the company's equipment continues to be adopted through DRAM generation transitions, building on its POR (Process of Record) track record in metal film processes, and adoption is expanding as customers launch new fabs. Firm NAND capital investment is expected, led by Japanese manufacturers.

quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): orders for ashing equipment for WLP (Wafer-Level Packaging) are expected to remain strong, supported by increased packaging production driven by growing GPU demand; management says its equipment is becoming the de facto standard in the descum process for WLP. It expects continued contributions from mass-production development investment in PLP (Panel-Level Packaging) by Taiwanese OSATs and Japanese manufacturers.

quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): power-device demand for AI and data-center applications remains strong, but because chips per wafer are approximately four times higher than for EV applications, customers can meet demand with existing capacity and it has not yet led to large-scale capital investment; the company is developing new material fields including GaN. Optical-device investment is expected to remain subdued after a large AR/VR project in China ran its course. Communications-device investment remains firm on the AI and data-center tailwind, with a conservative order forecast.

quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): Display - after strong orders from new-line G8 OLED investment by Chinese manufacturers and additional LCD investment, FY27/6 assumes some new-line LCD investment but no new OLED lines (additional equipment and modification work only), so a reactionary decline is expected; display-related production in China will be transferred and consolidated. Energy - roll-to-roll deposition equipment remains firm, supported partly by demand for capacitors used in AI and data-center applications; battery-related orders are expected at slightly less than JPY 1.0 billion, mainly development equipment, as resources shift to next-generation double-sided lithium deposition technology.
quarterly_data.figure: battery-related orders expected slightly less than JPY 1.0 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): rare-earth magnet production equipment orders increased mainly in the United States as customers moved into full-scale production expansion for supply-chain diversification, and the strong order trend is expected to continue; the plan's order forecast is conservative, while inquiry-level potential already exceeds JPY 20.0 billion. Management describes the equipment as a high-margin product.

quarterly_data.quarter: Ulvac results briefing Q&A: Key Q&A from FY26/6 Q4 Web Earnings Briefing (08-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): production-site restructuring and workforce optimization are expected to cut fixed costs by approximately JPY 2.0 billion this fiscal year. Current production capacity is sufficient for near-term demand but not for the JPY 360.0 billion net sales target for FY31/6, so the company is considering expansion investment at the Kyushu Plant, its main production site for semiconductor and electronic device equipment, while proceeding with the start of rare-earth-related equipment production at the Chigasaki Plant; it will complete the new production structure during FY27/6 and expects it to support sales and profit growth from FY28/6.
quarterly_data.figure: fixed-cost reduction approximately JPY 2.0 billion; FY31/6 net sales target JPY 360.0 billion
